questions.explanation: Recreates realistic team scenarios in the actual clinical environment with structured debriefing In situ simulation conducted in the real clinical setting reveals latent system hazards — missing equipment, unclear role assignment, communication breakdown — that laboratory simulation cannot. Structured debriefing is where learning consolidates; simulation without debriefing produces experience without insight. Team-based scenarios address the coordination failures that dominate serious safety events.

questions.text: An organization wants to increase safety event reporting. Which action is most likely to succeed? [App]

options.a: Setting a required minimum number of reports per unit
options.b: Providing timely feedback to reporters describing what was learned and what changed as a result
options.c: Making the reporting system anonymous only
options.d: Adding reporting compliance to annual performance evaluations

questions.explanation: Providing timely feedback to reporters describing what was learned and what changed as a result Staff stop reporting when reports appear to disappear. Closing the loop demonstrates that reporting produces change, which is the only durable incentive. Quotas (A) generate low-quality reports to meet a number. Anonymity alone (C) prevents follow-up clarification and does not address the feedback gap. Option D converts a learning behavior into a compliance obligation.

questions.text: Restraint use should be evaluated within a patient safety program because restraints [App]

options.a: Are expensive to maintain
options.b: Carry documented risks of physical and psychological harm and are subject to specific regulatory requirements
options.c: Increase nursing workload
options.d: Are prohibited in all healthcare settings

questions.explanation: Carry documented risks of physical and psychological harm and are subject to specific regulatory requirements Restraints are associated with injury, strangulation, aspiration, deconditioning, and psychological trauma, and CMS Conditions of Participation §482.13 impose detailed requirements for order, assessment, monitoring, and time limitation. Death associated with restraint use is a reportable event. Restraint reduction is therefore both a safety and a regulatory compliance priority.

questions.text: A safety huddle differs from a traditional shift report in that a safety huddle [R]

options.a: Is longer and more comprehensive
options.b: Is a brief, focused forward-looking review of anticipated safety risks for the coming period
options.c: Includes only nursing staff
options.d: Occurs weekly rather than daily

questions.explanation: Is a brief, focused forward-looking review of anticipated safety risks for the coming period The safety huddle is prospective — which patients are at highest risk, what equipment concerns exist, what staffing gaps are anticipated. Shift report is retrospective patient-by-patient handoff. Tiered daily safety huddles escalating from unit to department to executive level are a named high-reliability practice within the CMS Patient Safety Structural Measure.

questions.text: A patient safety event resulted in a prolonged hospital stay and required additional surgery, but the patient recovered fully. This is best classified as [App]

options.a: A near miss
options.b: An adverse event with temporary harm
options.c: A sentinel event with permanent harm
options.d: An unsafe condition

questions.explanation: An adverse event with temporary harm Harm occurred and required intervention, so this exceeds a near miss (A) and an unsafe condition (D). Because the patient recovered fully, permanent harm did not result. Note that severe temporary harm requiring major intervention may still meet an organization's sentinel event definition — classification systems vary in threshold, and organizational policy should define which events trigger comprehensive systematic analysis.

questions.text: Following an RCA, an action ranked as "weaker" in the RCA2 framework would be [App]

options.a: Eliminating a look-alike product from the formulary
options.b: Implementing a new policy and educating staff on it
options.c: Installing a physical barrier that prevents incorrect connection
options.d: Standardizing equipment across all units

questions.explanation: Implementing a new policy and educating staff on it The NPSF RCA2 framework classifies corrective actions as stronger, intermediate, or weaker by their dependence on human memory and vigilance. Policy and education are the archetypal weaker actions. Elimination (A) and physical barriers (C) are stronger; standardization (D) is intermediate. RCA2 recommends that every action plan include at least one stronger action rather than relying exclusively on weaker ones.

questions.text: A hospital's medication error rate increased following implementation of a new electronic ordering system. The most likely explanation is [An]

options.a: The system is defective and should be removed
options.b: Implementation introduced new error types while eliminating others, and workflow integration requires evaluation
options.c: Staff require disciplinary action for non-compliance
options.d: The prior paper system was safer overall

questions.explanation: Implementation introduced new error types while eliminating others, and workflow integration requires evaluation Health IT reliably eliminates certain error classes — illegible handwriting, transcription — while introducing others: selection from adjacent dropdown entries, alert fatigue, wrong-patient entry from multiple open records, and juxtaposition errors. This phenomenon, described as e-iatrogenesis, requires post-implementation surveillance and workflow adjustment rather than reversal or blame.

questions.text: Credentialing differs from privileging in that credentialing [R]

options.a: Determines which specific procedures a practitioner may perform
options.b: Verifies the practitioner's education, licensure, training, and experience
options.c: Occurs only at initial appointment
options.d: Is performed by the governing body directly

questions.explanation: Verifies the practitioner's education, licensure, training, and experience Credentialing establishes qualifications — who the practitioner is and what they are trained to do. Privileging is the subsequent decision granting authority to perform specific procedures at that organization, based on credentials plus demonstrated current competence. A practitioner can be fully credentialed yet denied a specific privilege for insufficient recent volume or outcomes.

questions.text: Primary source verification requires that [App]

options.a: The practitioner provides original documents
options.b: The organization confirms credentials directly with the issuing institution or an approved designated equivalent
options.c: Two staff members review the application
options.d: The medical staff office retains copies for five years

questions.explanation: The organization confirms credentials directly with the issuing institution or an approved designated equivalent Primary source verification means contacting the source that issued the credential — the medical school, residency program, or licensing board — rather than relying on documents the applicant supplies, which can be falsified. Approved designated equivalent sources, such as the AMA Physician Masterfile or credentials verification organizations, may substitute. This is an accreditation requirement across accrediting bodies.

questions.text: Medical staff bylaws function to [R]

options.a: Define the organization's strategic quality objectives
options.b: Establish the self-governance structure of the medical staff, including appointment, privileging, and peer review processes
options.c: Specify clinical treatment protocols
options.d: Set staffing ratios for clinical departments

questions.explanation: Establish the self-governance structure of the medical staff, including appointment, privileging, and peer review processes Bylaws are the constitutional document of the organized medical staff, required by CMS Conditions of Participation §482.22 and approved by the governing body. They define membership categories, officer roles, committee structure, credentialing and privileging procedures, corrective action processes, and the fair hearing rights afforded practitioners subject to adverse action.

questions.text: Concurrent utilization review is conducted [R]

options.a: Before the service is delivered
options.b: During the patient's stay, while care is ongoing
options.c: After discharge and claim submission
options.d: Only when a payer denies a claim

questions.explanation: During the patient's stay, while care is ongoing Utilization review occurs at three points: prospective, before service, addressing medical necessity and authorization; concurrent, during the stay, addressing continued stay appropriateness and level of care; and retrospective, after discharge, addressing claim review and pattern analysis. Concurrent review is the only point at which findings can still influence the care being delivered.

questions.text: Evidence-based medical necessity criteria sets such as InterQual or MCG are used to [App]

options.a: Determine the clinical treatment plan for the patient
options.b: Support consistent determination of appropriate level of care and continued stay
options.c: Establish the organization's charge structure
options.d: Replace physician clinical judgment

questions.explanation: Support consistent determination of appropriate level of care and continued stay These criteria sets standardize level-of-care determinations — inpatient versus observation, continued stay justification — reducing variation and supporting defensible documentation. They inform rather than replace physician judgment (D); when a case does not meet criteria but the physician believes admission is warranted, escalation to a physician advisor is the standard pathway.

questions.text: A physician advisor in utilization management primarily [R]

options.a: Provides direct patient care to complex patients
options.b: Reviews cases not meeting criteria and engages attending physicians on level of care and documentation
options.c: Approves all admissions to the hospital
options.d: Supervises the case management department

questions.explanation: Reviews cases not meeting criteria and engages attending physicians on level of care and documentation The physician advisor provides the peer-to-peer clinical judgment that non-physician reviewers cannot, both internally with attending physicians and externally with payer medical directors. The role is essential because level-of-care determination requires clinical reasoning about the specific patient, not mechanical criteria application.

questions.text: Clinical documentation integrity programs primarily aim to [App]

options.a: Reduce the volume of documentation clinicians must complete
options.b: Ensure the record accurately reflects the patient's clinical severity, supporting accurate coding, quality measurement, and risk adjustment
options.c: Increase reimbursement regardless of clinical accuracy
options.d: Standardize the format of physician notes

questions.explanation: Ensure the record accurately reflects the patient's clinical severity, supporting accurate coding, quality measurement, and risk adjustment CDI addresses the gap between clinical reality and documented specificity — when a physician documents "renal insufficiency" rather than the specific acute kidney injury stage, coding, risk adjustment, and quality measurement all understate severity. This affects observed-to-expected mortality ratios and case mix index alongside reimbursement. Option C describes upcoding, which carries False Claims Act exposure.

questions.text: A hospital's case mix index has declined over two quarters while patient acuity has not changed. The most likely explanation is [An]

options.a: Physicians are admitting healthier patients
options.b: Documentation and coding are not capturing existing clinical severity
options.c: The hospital has reduced its bed count
options.d: Payer contracts have changed

questions.explanation: Documentation and coding are not capturing existing clinical severity Case mix index reflects documented and coded severity, not clinical severity. When acuity is unchanged but CMI falls, the gap lies in capture — often following physician turnover, EHR template change, or CDI staffing reduction. Because CMI drives both reimbursement and the expected values in risk-adjusted outcome measures, undercapture makes an organization appear to perform worse than it does.

questions.text: Which is an element of an effective corporate compliance program per OIG guidance? [R]

options.a: Annual external financial audit only
options.b: Designated compliance officer, written standards, training, effective communication lines, auditing and monitoring, enforcement, and prompt response to detected offenses
options.c: Legal review of all contracts
options.d: Mandatory reporting of all events to the state health department

questions.explanation: Designated compliance officer, written standards, training, effective communication lines, auditing and monitoring, enforcement, and prompt response to detected offenses The Office of Inspector General's seven elements define an effective compliance program, and their presence is considered in enforcement decisions and settlement terms. Quality professionals intersect with compliance most directly through documentation integrity, quality-based payment program accuracy, and reportable event identification.

questions.text: The federal False Claims Act creates liability for [R]

options.a: Any billing error, regardless of intent
options.b: Knowingly submitting false or fraudulent claims for payment to the federal government
options.c: Failure to achieve quality performance targets
options.d: Delayed submission of quality data

questions.explanation: Knowingly submitting false or fraudulent claims for payment to the federal government The FCA requires knowledge, which includes actual knowledge, deliberate ignorance, and reckless disregard — but not simple negligence. It carries treble damages and per-claim penalties, and its qui tam provisions permit whistleblower suits with a share of recovery. Quality data submitted inaccurately to payment programs can fall within its scope, which is why data integrity carries legal as well as professional weight.

questions.text: The Stark Law prohibits [R]

options.a: Any financial relationship between hospitals and physicians
options.b: Physician referrals for designated health services to entities with which the physician has a financial relationship, absent an applicable exception
options.c: Payment of physician salaries above market rate
options.d: Physician ownership of medical equipment

questions.explanation: Physician referrals for designated health services to entities with which the physician has a financial relationship, absent an applicable exception Stark is a strict liability statute — intent is not required, which distinguishes it sharply from the Anti-Kickback Statute, where intent to induce referrals is an element. Because liability attaches without intent, compliance depends entirely on fitting each financial relationship within a defined exception, making documentation of fair market value and commercial reasonableness essential.

questions.text: External peer review is most appropriate when [App]

options.a: Routine OPPE data are being reviewed
options.b: Internal review presents a conflict of interest, the required specialty expertise is unavailable internally, or the case is highly complex or contested
options.c: A practitioner requests it
options.d: The volume of cases exceeds internal committee capacity

questions.explanation: Internal review presents a conflict of interest, the required specialty expertise is unavailable internally, or the case is highly complex or contested External review provides independence and specialty expertise where internal review would be compromised — a sole practitioner in a specialty with no internal peer, competing practitioners in the same market, or a case where internal findings are disputed. It strengthens the defensibility of any subsequent adverse action by demonstrating impartial evaluation.

questions.text: Under the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program, hospitals face payment reduction based on [R]

options.a: Total readmission volume
options.b: Excess readmission ratios for specified conditions, risk-adjusted and compared to national performance
options.c: The proportion of readmissions occurring within 7 days
options.d: Patient satisfaction with discharge instructions

questions.explanation: Excess readmission ratios for specified conditions, risk-adjusted and compared to national performance HRRP calculates excess readmission ratios as predicted over expected readmissions for specified conditions, risk-adjusted for patient characteristics, with penalties applied to base operating DRG payments. Because the comparison is national and relative, a hospital can improve its absolute rate and still incur a penalty if peers improved more — a feature quality professionals must explain to leadership.

questions.text: Quality improvement records retained beyond the organizational retention schedule create risk primarily because [App]

options.a: Storage costs increase
options.b: Records outside the retention policy may be discoverable and can conflict with the organization's stated practice
options.c: Accreditors require destruction after a defined period
options.d: Older records are less accurate

questions.explanation: Records outside the retention policy may be discoverable and can conflict with the organization's stated practice Inconsistent retention practice undermines the defensibility of the retention policy itself and can produce records in litigation that the organization asserted no longer existed. Task 6.C requires maintaining confidentiality of performance and quality improvement records, and consistent application of a defined, legally reviewed schedule is part of that obligation.

questions.text: A payer denies a claim for inpatient admission on the basis that observation status was appropriate. The quality professional's most useful contribution is [App]

options.a: Instructing the physician to change the documented level of care
options.b: Analyzing denial patterns to identify systemic documentation or utilization review gaps and addressing them upstream
options.c: Accepting the denial to preserve the payer relationship
options.d: Appealing every denial without review

questions.explanation: Analyzing denial patterns to identify systemic documentation or utilization review gaps and addressing them upstream Individual denials are managed by revenue cycle and physician advisors; the quality professional's distinctive value is pattern analysis identifying whether denials cluster by service, physician, or documentation element — converting a recurring financial loss into a correctable process defect. Option A is documentation alteration, which carries compliance exposure.

questions.text: Which best demonstrates evaluation of compliance with clinical practice guidelines? [App]

options.a: Confirming the guideline is posted on the intranet
options.b: Measuring the proportion of eligible patients whose care conformed to guideline recommendations, with analysis of documented variance
options.c: Tracking the number of physicians who attended the guideline rollout
options.d: Counting guideline downloads from the intranet

questions.explanation: Measuring the proportion of eligible patients whose care conformed to guideline recommendations, with analysis of documented variance Task 6.B.1 requires evaluating compliance with requirements for clinical practice guidelines, pathways, and outcomes. Genuine evaluation measures conformance in actual cases and examines variance — importantly, justified clinical variance is expected and appropriate, so the analysis must distinguish documented clinical exception from unexplained deviation. Options A, C, and D measure availability and exposure.

questions.text: CMS Conditions of Participation establish [R]

options.a: Voluntary best practice recommendations
options.b: Minimum health and safety requirements that providers must meet to participate in Medicare and Medicaid
options.c: Accreditation standards for private accrediting bodies
options.d: Payment rates for covered services

questions.explanation: Minimum health and safety requirements that providers must meet to participate in Medicare and Medicaid The CoPs are federal regulations establishing the floor for program participation, enforced through state survey agencies or through accreditors holding deeming authority. They are mandatory, not aspirational. Accreditation standards may exceed CoP requirements but cannot fall below them — a deemed accreditor's standards must be determined by CMS to be equivalent or more stringent.

questions.text: A finding of immediate jeopardy means that [App]

options.a: A minor standard-level deficiency was identified
options.b: A situation has caused or is likely to cause serious injury, harm, impairment, or death to a patient, requiring immediate corrective action
options.c: The organization must close within 30 days
options.d: Accreditation is automatically revoked

questions.explanation: A situation has caused or is likely to cause serious injury, harm, impairment, or death to a patient, requiring immediate corrective action Immediate jeopardy is the most serious survey finding, triggering an abbreviated timeline for removal of the jeopardy — typically requiring an acceptable removal plan within days — and, if unresolved, termination from the Medicare program. It requires immediate action to abate the hazard, followed by a plan of correction addressing the underlying systemic cause.

questions.text: A plan of correction submitted following a regulatory survey should include [R]

options.a: A statement disputing the surveyor's findings
options.b: The corrective action, how compliance will be monitored, who is responsible, and the completion date
options.c: A list of staff involved in the deficient practice
options.d: A request for extension of the compliance timeline

questions.explanation: The corrective action, how compliance will be monitored, who is responsible, and the completion date An acceptable plan of correction must address how the specific deficiency will be corrected, how other patients potentially affected will be identified and protected, what systemic changes will prevent recurrence, how monitoring will verify sustained compliance, and who is accountable by what date. Plans limited to correcting the individual instance without systemic change are routinely rejected.

questions.text: CLIA regulations govern [R]

options.a: Hospital emergency department operations
options.b: Laboratory testing performed on human specimens for health assessment purposes
options.c: Medical device manufacturing
options.d: Pharmacy compounding practices

questions.explanation: Laboratory testing performed on human specimens for health assessment purposes The Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 establish federal quality standards for all laboratory testing on human specimens, categorized by test complexity — waived, moderate, and high complexity — with proportionate requirements for personnel qualifications, proficiency testing, and quality control. CLIA applies to point-of-care testing in clinics and units, which organizations frequently overlook.

questions.text: An organization pursuing accreditation through DNV using ISO 9001 integration differs from a traditional accreditation approach in that it [App]

options.a: Does not require compliance with CMS Conditions of Participation
options.b: Integrates a quality management system standard with annual survey, emphasizing systematic process management
options.c: Eliminates the need for internal quality monitoring
options.d: Applies only to critical access hospitals

questions.explanation: Integrates a quality management system standard with annual survey, emphasizing systematic process management DNV's approach pairs CMS-deemed hospital accreditation with ISO 9001 quality management system requirements, surveying annually rather than at longer intervals. All deemed accreditors must ensure CoP compliance (A is incorrect regardless of accreditor). Task 7.A requires evaluating accreditation options, and survey frequency, standards philosophy, and cost all factor into the selection.

questions.text: Promoting awareness of statutory and regulatory requirements throughout an organization is most effectively achieved by [App]

options.a: Distributing the full regulatory text to all departments
options.b: Translating requirements into role-specific expectations embedded in workflows, orientation, and competency validation
options.c: Posting regulatory updates on the organizational intranet
options.d: Requiring annual compliance attestation from all staff

questions.explanation: Translating requirements into role-specific expectations embedded in workflows, orientation, and competency validation Task 7.B requires promoting awareness of statutory and regulatory requirements within the organization. Awareness that changes behavior requires translation — staff need to know what a requirement means for their specific work, not the regulation's text. Options A, C, and D deliver information or attestation without conversion into practice.

questions.text: A validation survey conducted by a state survey agency at a deemed-status hospital serves to [R]

options.a: Replace the accreditation survey
options.b: Verify that the accrediting organization's survey process adequately identifies CoP noncompliance
options.c: Determine the hospital's payment rate
options.d: Investigate a specific patient complaint

questions.explanation: Verify that the accrediting organization's survey process adequately identifies CoP noncompliance CMS conducts validation surveys on a sample of deemed facilities to assess whether the accreditor's process reliably detects CoP deficiencies. Poor validation performance can jeopardize an accreditor's deeming authority. This is distinct from a complaint survey (D), which investigates a specific allegation and can occur at any accredited facility.

questions.text: Which action best supports ongoing monitoring of compliance with organizational, state, and federal requirements? [App]

options.a: Reviewing requirements immediately before each scheduled survey
options.b: Maintaining a regulatory requirement inventory with assigned owners and a scheduled audit calendar
options.c: Relying on accreditor findings to identify noncompliance
options.d: Delegating all compliance monitoring to the legal department

questions.explanation: Maintaining a regulatory requirement inventory with assigned owners and a scheduled audit calendar Task 7.C requires supporting processes for evaluating, monitoring, and improving compliance with organizational, state, and federal requirements. An inventory with named owners and scheduled audits converts compliance from an episodic scramble into a managed program with visible status. Option C is definitionally reactive — it uses external survey as the detection mechanism, meaning noncompliance is discovered by the regulator rather than the organization. Emerging content forecast for the unscored pretest pool. Lower confidence by design. P1. The Age-Friendly Health Systems 4Ms framework comprises [R] A. Medication, Mentation, Mobility, and What Matters B. Measurement, Monitoring, Management, and Mitigation C. Mortality, Morbidity, Mobility, and Medication D. Mission, Method, Measurement, and Mastery ✅ Correct Answer: A — Medication, Mentation, Mobility, and What Matters The 4Ms framework, developed by IHI with The John A. Hartford Foundation, structures care for older adults around four evidence-based elements. "What Matters" is placed first in most representations because the patient's own goals should govern how the other three are managed. CMS has introduced an Age-Friendly Hospital structural measure, raising the framework's measurement relevance. P2. Perinatal safety bundles typically address [App] A. Neonatal intensive care staffing ratios B. Standardized responses to obstetric hemorrhage, severe hypertension, and other leading causes of maternal morbidity C. Prenatal genetic screening protocols D. Labor and delivery unit design ✅ Correct Answer: B — Standardized responses to obstetric hemorrhage, severe hypertension, and other leading causes of maternal morbidity Patient safety bundles from the Alliance for Innovation on Maternal Health structure each around readiness, recognition, response, and reporting/systems learning. Severe maternal morbidity and its documented racial disparities have become a national quality priority, with CMS maternal health measures and TJC perinatal safety standards both in force. P3. The CMS SEP-1 sepsis measure is best characterized as [R] A. An outcome measure of sepsis mortality B. A process bundle measure requiring completion of specified elements within defined time windows C. A structural measure of sepsis program presence D. A patient-reported outcome measure ✅ Correct Answer: B — A process bundle measure requiring completion of specified elements within defined time windows SEP-1 is an all-or-none bundle measure — every required element within the specified window must be documented for the case to pass, meaning a single missed element fails the entire case. This construction makes performance highly sensitive to documentation as well as care delivery. SEP-1 has been incorporated into value-based purchasing, raising its financial significance. P4. Health-related social needs screening differs from social determinants of health in that health-related social needs are [R] A. Identical concepts with different terminology B. The individual-level, immediate, actionable needs a specific patient reports, while SDOH are the population-level conditions producing them C. Assessed only in inpatient settings D. Reported to public health authorities ✅ Correct Answer: B — The individual-level, immediate, actionable needs a specific patient reports, while SDOH are the population-level conditions producing them The distinction matters operationally. A patient reporting they cannot afford food this week has a health-related social need addressable by referral. Food insecurity across a community is a social determinant addressable through policy and partnership. Confusing the levels produces either individual referrals with no community strategy or community strategy with no patient-level response. P5. A ransomware attack that disables a hospital's electronic health record should be understood primarily as [App] A. An information technology issue outside quality's scope B. A patient safety event requiring downtime procedures, clinical risk mitigation, and post-event analysis C. A financial loss event D. A public relations matter ✅ Correct Answer: B — A patient safety event requiring downtime procedures, clinical risk mitigation, and post-event analysis Extended EHR unavailability degrades medication safety, allergy checking, results reporting, and clinical decision support simultaneously, with documented increases in mortality and adverse events during prolonged outages. Cybersecurity has consequently entered the patient safety domain, requiring tested downtime procedures, clinical continuity planning, and post-event systematic analysis. P6. A patient and family advisory council contributes most effectively to quality when it [App] A. Reviews individual patient complaints B. Participates in design of care processes, materials, and improvement initiatives before decisions are finalized C. Meets annually to receive an organizational update D. Is composed of former employees ✅ Correct Answer: B — Participates in design of care processes, materials, and improvement initiatives before decisions are finalized PFACs generate value through upstream involvement — patients and families identify usability failures, communication gaps, and dignity concerns that clinical designers reliably miss. Councils confined to receiving updates (C) or reviewing individual complaints (A) function as advisory theater. Patient and family engagement is a named domain in the CMS Patient Safety Structural Measure. P7. Under MACRA's Merit-based Incentive Payment System, clinician performance is assessed across [R] A. Quality only B. Quality, cost, improvement activities, and promoting interoperability C. Patient satisfaction and cost only D. Volume and cost ✅ Correct Answer: B — Quality, cost, improvement activities, and promoting interoperability MIPS combines four weighted performance categories into a composite score determining a positive, neutral, or negative payment adjustment applied on a two-year lag. Category weights have shifted over program years, with cost weighting increasing. MIPS Value Pathways represent CMS's effort to move toward more cohesive, specialty-aligned measure sets. P8. Hospital price transparency requirements obligate hospitals to [R] A. Publish only their charge master B. Publish a machine-readable file of standard charges and a consumer-friendly display of shoppable services C. Provide individual price estimates on request only D. Match competitor pricing ✅ Correct Answer: B — Publish a machine-readable file of standard charges and a consumer-friendly display of shoppable services CMS requires both a comprehensive machine-readable file including gross charges, payer-specific negotiated rates, discounted cash prices, and de-identified minimum and maximum negotiated charges, plus a consumer-facing display of shoppable services. Noncompliance carries civil monetary penalties scaled to hospital size, and compliance is a defined regulatory obligation under Task 7.C. P9. An organization implements an AI-based ambient documentation tool. The most important quality safeguard is [App] A. Selecting the tool with the fastest processing speed B. Clinician review and attestation of generated documentation before it enters the legal record C. Requiring all clinicians to adopt the tool simultaneously D. Disabling the tool for complex patients ✅ Correct Answer: B — Clinician review and attestation of generated documentation before it enters the legal record Ambient documentation tools can omit, misattribute, or fabricate clinical content. Because the record is the legal and clinical record of care and the substrate for quality measurement and billing, clinician verification before finalization is the essential control. Documentation errors propagate into coding, risk adjustment, and downstream clinical decisions. P10. Diagnostic safety measurement is challenging primarily because [An] A. Diagnostic errors are rare B. Diagnosis unfolds over time across settings, and errors are often identified only retrospectively, making case identification difficult C. Clinicians resist measurement D. No definition of diagnostic error exists ✅ Correct Answer: B — Diagnosis unfolds over time across settings, and errors are often identified only retrospectively, making case identification difficult Unlike a wrong-site surgery, a missed diagnosis has no discrete event moment — it emerges across encounters, often in different organizations, and may surface only when the patient deteriorates. Trigger-based approaches such as reviewing unplanned returns within short intervals, and structured tools such as SAFER Dx, are the emerging measurement strategies. P11. In an episode-based payment model, a hospital's most direct lever for improving performance is [App] A. Reducing inpatient length of stay only B. Managing post-acute care utilization and readmissions across the full episode window C. Increasing surgical volume D. Renegotiating supply contracts ✅ Correct Answer: B — Managing post-acute care utilization and readmissions across the full episode window In episode models, post-acute care placement and readmissions typically account for the largest share of variation in total episode cost. Discharging to home with home health rather than to a skilled nursing facility, where clinically appropriate, produces larger effects than inpatient efficiency gains. This makes care transition quality directly financially consequential. P12. Environmental sustainability in healthcare connects to quality primarily through [App] A. Reduced operating expenses B. The health effects on served communities of emissions, waste, and resource use, linking organizational operations to population health outcomes C. Improved public perception D. Accreditation requirements ✅ Correct Answer: B — The health effects on served communities of emissions, waste, and resource use, linking organizational operations to population health outcomes The health sector's environmental footprint contributes to air quality, heat exposure, and extreme weather effects that produce measurable morbidity in the communities health systems serve — creating an internal contradiction between organizational operations and population health mission. This positions sustainability within Module 3 accountability rather than as a separate facilities concern. P13. A hospital's quality committee is reviewing whether to adopt a newly published predictive model for sepsis. The most important question to ask is [An] A. How many other hospitals have adopted it B. What population it was validated in, how it performs in populations resembling ours, and what actions its alerts will trigger C. What the licensing cost is D. Which vendor developed it ✅ Correct Answer: B — What population it was validated in, how it performs in populations resembling ours, and what actions its alerts will trigger Model performance degrades when the deployment population differs from the development population in prevalence, demographics, or documentation practice. Equally important is the action question — an alert that triggers no defined clinical response produces alert burden without benefit. Local validation and a defined response protocol are the two prerequisites to safe deployment. P14. Workforce well-being is increasingly measured within quality programs because [App] A. It is required for accreditation B. Burnout and staffing instability are associated with increased adverse events, reduced patient experience, and turnover C. It reduces recruitment expense D. It is a human resources performance indicator ✅ Correct Answer: B — Burnout and staffing instability are associated with increased adverse events, reduced patient experience, and turnover The evidence linking clinician burnout to error rates, reduced empathy, and attrition establishes workforce well-being as a patient safety variable rather than solely an employment concern. The National Academy of Medicine frames it as a systems issue, and it appears within patient safety frameworks including the CMS Patient Safety Structural Measure. P15. Digital quality measurement is expected to change quality programs primarily by [App] A. Eliminating the need for quality professionals B. Shifting measurement from sampled manual abstraction toward full-population automated calculation, moving the professional's work toward interpretation and improvement C. Reducing the number of measures reported D. Removing the need for risk adjustment ✅ Correct Answer: B — Shifting measurement from sampled manual abstraction toward full-population automated calculation, moving the professional's work toward interpretation and improvement Digital measurement removes the abstraction bottleneck and expands denominators from samples to full populations, improving precision and enabling stratification. The professional's work shifts upstream toward specification governance and documentation workflow design, and downstream toward interpretation and improvement — with risk adjustment (D) becoming more important, not less, as comparison becomes more granular.
